title: Adopt both SPEC amendments; narrow the fork tripwire to the routing surface after a K9 conflict
context: Two amendments were put to the user with costed options. First, section 6.2 gives both reviewers the invariant "a diff exists", which checks the artifact and not the criteria, so a brief naming criteria that resolve only in the calling conversation passes and the agent reviews against invented standards. Second, nothing prevented a future edit reintroducing fork as a route, since the removal was a deleted sentence with no paired mechanism, unlike delivery-lead whose deletion is paired with the depth limit.U+000AU+000AThe user answered "proceed as recommended", selecting A for the reviewer clause and A+ for the fork census.U+000AU+000AApplying A+ surfaced a contradiction the options analysis had missed. A+ scoped the bare-word grep over ~/.claude/skills as well, but authoring standard K9 permits `context: fork` on a skill carrying an actionable task - a skill execution mode, not a routing choice. A bare-word census over the skills tree would forbid a field this spec's own standard allows, and the only way to keep the wider scope would be a phrasing exception, which is the sampled allowlist section 0.3 forbids.
options: A for reviewers: extend the entry invariant to 'every standard named in the brief resolves to a path', class M because the agent halts.
A+ for the census: bare-word grep over rules, agents, CLAUDE.md and skills.
A for the census: the same grep scoped to rules, agents and CLAUDE.md only, excluding the skills tree.
C for the census: match routing phrasings rather than the bare word - rejected as a sampled allowlist under section 0.3.
outcome: Both amendments adopted. The reviewer clause landed as A, unchanged from what was approved.U+000AU+000AThe fork census landed at A scope, not A+: `grep -rniE '\bfork' ~/.claude/rules ~/.claude/agents ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md | wc -l` returns 0, with the skills tree excluded. This narrows what the user approved, and the reason is recorded in section 8 of the SPEC rather than left implicit: K9 permits `context: fork`, so scope stops at the routing surface where the word has exactly one meaning. Measured 0 today across all four locations including skills, so the narrowing costs no coverage that currently exists.U+000AU+000ARecorded as open rather than assumed: whether `context: fork` on a skill is gated by the same server-side flag as the fork subagent type. If it is, a skill using it behaves differently across the two surfaces and K9 needs the same treatment section 11 gives the subagent type. Untested.U+000AU+000AApplying the amendments also caught three stale fork references the options analysis had not predicted. One was load-bearing: the machinist frontmatter in section 3.3 ended "do the work here or fork", which is literal config text destined for ~/.claude/agents/machinist.md and would have failed check 8.14 on the first run. The other two were section 1.2 citing fork as a live benefit of skills, and section 10.1 naming fork as a routing outcome. All three corrected.U+000AU+000ALanded as three commits on branch docs/agent-architecture-spec, cut from origin/main: 1395de13 lands SPEC revision 2 verbatim so the amendments are reviewable as a diff, 8a4e6f7a is revision 3 carrying 19 asserted single-match edits, 78a41bd0 is the implementation plan.
